No test is visible for this file.

terms.meaning: a set of questions used to learn about a company before building a model
a label that places a company in an industry and business type
a record of earlier messages in a chat, so the model can refer back to them

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File purpose and imports
sections.what: Describes an agent that asks questions to learn about a company before modelling. Brings in the base agent and logging.
sections.why: Likely reason: modelling needs company facts the user may not have typed in.
sections.watch_out: Only the question steps are visible here; no loop that asks and records answers is present in this file.

sections.name: QuestionnaireAgent (part 1)
sections.title: Setting up and writing the first questions
sections.what: Creates the agent with a conversation list that is set up but never filled in the visible code. Builds instructions asking for five to seven questions about products, revenue, business model, stage, costs, and growth, then sends them with the company name and optional description.
sections.why: Likely reason: the model writes the questions so they suit the specific company.
sections.watch_out: The conversation history is created empty and no visible code adds to it, so the agent has no memory of earlier answers.

sections.name: QuestionnaireAgent (part 2)
sections.title: Reading the questions and a standard backup
sections.what: Tries to read the model's answer as JSON and adds the prompt, model name, and time taken. If reading fails, returns five standard questions with the company name filled in.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app always has questions to show, even when the model's answer is messy.
sections.watch_out: When the model call fails, the standard questions are returned as if they came from the model, with the raw text attached.

sections.name: QuestionnaireAgent: analyze_answers_and_classify
sections.title: Classifying the interview answers
sections.what: Builds the list of question and answer pairs and asks the model to classify the company's industry, business and revenue model, stage, key insights, comparable companies, and a confidence score.
sections.why: Turns interview answers into the labels the rest of the workflow uses.
sections.watch_out: The confidence score is the model's own estimate, not a measured accuracy.

sections.name: QuestionnaireAgent (part 4)
sections.title: Reading the classification and starting the input list
sections.what: Reads the classification as JSON, or falls back to an Unknown industry with the raw text. Then starts the request for the financial inputs needed for this type of company, with the classification and context attached.
sections.why: Likely reason: the input list is generated from the company type so the form fits the business.
sections.watch_out: The fallback sets the industry to Unknown, which later steps may treat as a real industry.

sections.name: QuestionnaireAgent (part 5)
sections.title: Reading the required inputs
sections.what: Sends the input-list request, tries to read the answer as JSON, and records the prompt and timing. If reading fails, returns an empty list of inputs with the raw text.
sections.why: Keeps the prompt and raw text so a user can see what was asked and what came back.
sections.watch_out: An empty input list on failure looks like the company needs no inputs, which can hide a real problem.

summary: Agent that writes interview questions about a company, classifies the answers, and lists the financial inputs the model will need.
purpose: Helps a user describe a company in plain answers so the model builder can be set up for that kind of business.
why: Likely reason: a financial model fits better when the business type is known first.
how: Asks the model for five to seven questions. After answers are given, it sends the question and answer pairs to the model for a classification. Then it asks for a list of inputs needed for that type of company. Each step reads the answer as JSON and falls back to basic content if reading fails.
inputs: Company name, an optional description, question and answer pairs, and the classification from earlier steps.
outputs: Dictionaries holding questions, a classification, and a list of required inputs. Each includes the prompt used, and raw text when reading failed.
risks: Failed model calls return standard questions or empty lists as if they were real output. The conversation history is set up but not filled in the visible code. An Unknown industry label can flow into later steps.
debug: If questions look generic, the model call probably failed; check raw_response. Confirm the provider and model in settings. If the input list is empty, read the raw_response text from that step.
